purpose: Distinguish pending-input TAP gating from exhausted expansion credits at the eight-lane release throughput ceiling.
kernel: Linux 6.8.0-149-generic #149-Ubuntu SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Fri Oct 23 13:21:10 UTC 2026 x86_64
sequence: Baseline, diagnostic, baseline; 4 Gbit/s requested per direction then unlimited, twenty seconds per point.
validation: 349 ordinary release tests, strict all-target Clippy and formatting; focused diagnostic test, 82 kernel tests and all three unchanged runtime tests (101.20 s) on Linux 6.8. Diagnostic not revalidated on Linux 7.0; production baseline was.
limitations: Turn-boundary samples classify time until the next observation; intervals include preemption and the counter drain period, exclude unsampled endpoints, and are not exact source residence times.
Gate spare-credit and expansion-stalled measurements are independent subsets, not additive classes. Time sums across worker/session queues can exceed wall time.
The gate does not reveal the identities of unread TAP frames. Cross-flow interference follows from queue sharing, not direct observation of unread data.
Instrumentation adds snapshot and per-turn work and is not a production optimization.
No local builds, kernel tests or Git packing overlapped these throughput measurements.

Source inspection narrows compact-header GSO expansion failure to frame credit or Store capacity. In this single-session configuration, a pending source consumes a session credit, so session credit must bind before all view slots are occupied; that reason was not separately counted.
